name: publish-on-tag

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  publish-to-npm:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write # Required for OIDC Trusted Publishing.
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          cache: npm
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      - name: Update npm for OIDC Trusted Publishing
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run lint, tests, and build
        run: |
          npm run check
          npm test
          npm run build

      - name: Stage package on npm
        run: npm stage publish --provenance --access public

# Trace Engine CLI (`trace-engine-cli`) A fast, standalone, token-efficient command-line tool built on top of Chrome DevTools Trace Engine. It inspects Chromium performance traces (`.json` or `.json.gz`) and converts them into structured, high-signal summaries optimized for LLM context windows, AI coding agents, and developer performance diagnostics. --- ## Why `trace-engine-cli`? Raw Chromium performance traces are massive (often 20MB–200MB+ uncompressed), containing millions of low-level JSON events. Feeding raw traces directly to an LLM quickly exhausts token limits, incurs high costs, and drowns the model in noise. `trace-engine-cli` solves this by: - **Token Compression**: Reduces trace context sizes by up to **95%+** through domain-specific extractors and tabular **TOON** (Token-Oriented Object Notation) serialization. - **Chrome DevTools Trace Engine Integration**: Uses Chrome DevTools' battle-tested Trace Engine (`@paulirish/trace_engine`) to compute exact Core Web Vitals, task trees, and insight models. - **Relative Timeline Model**: Defaults to elapsed time from trace start (`0ms`), matching the DevTools Performance panel timeline ruler and eliminating timestamp calculation errors. - **Progressive Drill-Down**: Guides agents and humans from high-level summaries (`overview`) down into specific performance bottlenecks (`insights`, `tasks`, `find`, `profile`, `diff`, `scheduling`, `network`, `interactions`, `shifts`, `events`, `navigations`, `scan`). - **Flexible Engine Resolution**: Uses `@paulirish/trace_engine` by default, or bundles single-file trace engine artifacts directly from local `devtools-frontend` checkouts. --- ## Installation Install [`trace-engine-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/trace-engine-cli) globally from npm to add `trace-engine-cli` to your `$PATH`: ```bash npm install -g trace-engine-cli trace-engine-cli /path/to/trace.json.gz ``` Or run it directly with `npx`: ```bash npx trace-engine-cli /path/to/trace.json.gz ``` --- ## Using with AI Coding Agents `trace-engine-cli` is designed for progressive self-discovery so AI coding agents can learn its capabilities at runtime without loading the entire manual into your system prompt. ### How Agents Discover Capabilities 1. **Default overview + built-in drill-down hints (`trace-engine-cli `)**: Calling `trace-engine-cli ` with no subcommand runs `overview` and appends a `# Drill-down commands:` reference footer to the output. That first call gives the agent the trace bounds, Core Web Vitals, main-thread category breakdown, and the exact syntax for every follow-up subcommand. 2. **Top-level command discovery (`trace-engine-cli` or `trace-engine-cli --help`)**: Running `trace-engine-cli` with no arguments or passing `--help` prints all 13 subcommands (`overview`, `insights`, `tasks`, `find`, `profile`, `diff`, `scheduling`, `network`, `interactions`, `shifts`, `events`, `navigations`, `scan`) and global options. 3. **Subcommand flag discovery (`trace-engine-cli --help`)**: Running `--help` on any subcommand (for example, `trace-engine-cli insights --help` or `trace-engine-cli events --help`) prints the flags, choices, and defaults for that command. ### Option 1: Minimal `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` Rule Add this snippet to your project instruction file (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `.cursorrules`) to stop your agent from writing ad-hoc JSON parsing scripts and direct it to `trace-engine-cli`: ```markdown ## Performance Trace Analysis (`.json`, `.json.gz`) - Never parse or search trace files manually with `jq`, `python`, `node -e`, `zcat`, or shell loops. Use `trace-engine-cli`, which handles gzip decompression, DevTools Trace Engine parsing, and token-compact TOON formatting. - Start any single-trace investigation by running `trace-engine-cli `. Read the overview and the `# Drill-down commands:` footer appended to the output to choose follow-up commands. - To search across multiple trace files or directories, run `trace-engine-cli scan [options]`. - Run `trace-engine-cli --help` or `trace-engine-cli --help` to inspect available subcommands and flags. ``` ### Option 2: Agent Skill Template (`SKILL.md`) If your agent environment supports on-demand skills (such as `.gemini/skills/chrome-trace-analysis/SKILL.md` or `.claude/skills/chrome-trace-analysis/SKILL.md`), expand the block below and copy the template:
Click to view full SKILL.md template ````markdown --- name: chrome-trace-analysis description: Inspect and query Chrome/DevTools performance trace files and test fixtures (.json, .json.gz) using trace-engine-cli. Use when analyzing trace events, insights, or fixtures. --- # Chrome & Chromium DevTools Trace Analysis Use `trace-engine-cli` to inspect, profile, and diagnose performance recordings captured by the Chrome/Chromium DevTools Performance panel (`.json`, `.json.gz`). --- ## 1. Operational Constraints - **Never parse or search traces manually**: Do not write ad-hoc `node -e`, `python`, `jq`, `zcat`, `gzcat`, `zgrep`, `zless`, or shell loops to inspect or search trace files or fixtures. `trace-engine-cli` handles gzip decompression, multi-file scanning, trace engine parsing, model traversal, and formatting. - **Check command help proactively**: Run `trace-engine-cli --help` or `trace-engine-cli --help` to view available commands, flags (`--time-range`, `--category`, `--function`, `--top`), and output options before attempting custom workarounds. --- ## 2. Core Principles - **Relative by default**: Time ranges (`--time-range`, `--window-a`, `--window-b`) default to relative time from trace start (`0ms` origin), matching the DevTools Performance panel UI. - **Time units**: Range arguments accept milliseconds or explicit unit suffixes (`3500,4200`, `3.5s,4.2s`, `100ms,500ms`). - **Absolute timestamps**: Pass `--absolute-timestamps` when querying raw epoch timestamps. - **Output format**: Use `--format toon` (compact YAML-like output, default) for token efficiency, or `--format md` when generating Markdown tables for reports. --- ## 3. Command Reference ### `trace-engine-cli ` / `trace-engine-cli overview ` High-level trace metadata, duration, Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), and main-thread category breakdown (Scripting, Layout, Rendering, GC, System, Idle). Calling `trace-engine-cli ` without `overview` also prints the `# Drill-down commands:` reference footer. ```bash trace-engine-cli trace.json.gz ``` ### `trace-engine-cli insights ` Diagnostic insight cards for Core Web Vitals and performance bottlenecks. ```bash trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz # Filter by diagnostic category: lcp, inp, cls, render-blocking, third-parties trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category cls # Target a specific navigation ID or InsightSet ID trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --navigation NAVIGATION_0 ``` ### `trace-engine-cli shifts ` Layout shift clusters, scores, and culprit DOM elements. ```bash # Cluster summary trace-engine-cli shifts trace.json.gz # Include individual shift events, navigation IDs, and impacted DOM nodes trace-engine-cli shifts trace.json.gz --events ``` ### `trace-engine-cli events ` Inspect and filter raw trace events by name, category, phase, time range, or extract payload fields via dot notation. ```bash # Match specific event names trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --name LayoutShift,navigationStart # Extract nested payload fields via dot notation trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --name LayoutShift --fields args.data.navigationId,args.data.score # Filter by category and phase trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --cat devtools.timeline --phase X --top 20 ``` ### `trace-engine-cli navigations ` (alias: `navs`) List all navigations in the trace, their primary main frame status, and their mapped Chrome DevTools Trace Engine `InsightSet` IDs. ```bash trace-engine-cli navigations trace.json.gz ``` ### `trace-engine-cli profile ` Time-bucketed CPU profiling progression across discrete intervals. ```bash trace-engine-cli profile trace.json.gz --time-range "3500,4200" --top 3 trace-engine-cli profile trace.json.gz --time-range "3s,5s" --bucket 50ms ``` ### `trace-engine-cli find ` Search for function execution instances, call frequency, and execution times. ```bash trace-engine-cli find trace.json.gz --function "drawEventTiles" --time-range "3000,5000" ``` ### `trace-engine-cli tasks ` Inspect long tasks (>50ms) with bottom-up and top-down TraceTree call aggregations. ```bash trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz --time-range "0,5000" trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz --tree bottom-up --top 20 ``` ### `trace-engine-cli interactions ` List user interaction events, duration, processing delays, presentation delays, and target DOM elements. ```bash trace-engine-cli interactions trace.json.gz ``` ### `trace-engine-cli scheduling ` Detect `requestAnimationFrame` and `setTimeout` scheduling, cancellations, and churn loops. ```bash trace-engine-cli scheduling trace.json.gz --time-range "3500,4200" ``` ### `trace-engine-cli network ` Network request waterfall, timings, and initiator chains. ```bash trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --slowest 10 trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --render-blocking trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --initiator-chain "example.com" ``` ### `trace-engine-cli diff ` Differential CPU profile comparing two time windows. ```bash trace-engine-cli diff trace.json.gz --window-a "3500,4000" --window-b "4000,4200" --top 10 ``` ### `trace-engine-cli scan ` Scan a directory of trace files, a glob pattern, or multiple fixtures for matching events, categories, phases, or raw text patterns without loading heavyweight engine pipelines. ```bash # Scan a directory to find which fixture contains an event trace-engine-cli scan front_end/panels/timeline/fixtures/traces/ --name "LayerTreeHostImpl:snapshot" # Fast substring search across compressed traces trace-engine-cli scan "fixtures/**/*.json.gz" --grep "LayerTreeHostImpl" # Filter by category and phase across multiple files trace-engine-cli scan fixtures/traces/ --cat devtools.timeline --phase X ``` --- ## 4. Diagnostic Investigation Recipes ### Recipe A: Investigating UI Jank / Interaction Stalls 1. **Check scheduling churn**: `trace-engine-cli scheduling --time-range ","` 2. **Bucket CPU activity**: `trace-engine-cli profile --time-range ","` 3. **Check for starved functions**: `trace-engine-cli find --function "" --time-range ","` 4. **Diff against unblocked interval**: `trace-engine-cli diff --window-a "" --window-b ""` ### Recipe B: Diagnosing Core Web Vitals (INP / LCP / CLS) 1. Run `trace-engine-cli ` to inspect CWV scores. 2. If INP is poor, run `trace-engine-cli interactions `. 3. If CLS is high, run `trace-engine-cli shifts --events` and `trace-engine-cli insights --category cls`. 4. Run `trace-engine-cli insights ` for all diagnostic insight cards. ### Recipe C: Inspecting Test Fixtures (e.g. `fixtures/traces/`) 1. Check high-level trace contents: `trace-engine-cli ` 2. Inspect navigations and insight set IDs: `trace-engine-cli navigations ` 3. Inspect relevant subsystem: `trace-engine-cli shifts --events`, `trace-engine-cli network `, or `trace-engine-cli insights --category ` 4. Inspect raw event payloads: `trace-engine-cli events --name --fields ` ````
--- ## Quick Start Invoking `trace-engine-cli` with a trace file path runs the `overview` command and appends the `# Drill-down commands:` reference footer: ```bash # Default overview + drill-down hints in TOON format (optimized for LLMs) trace-engine-cli trace.json.gz # Overview in Markdown format (optimized for humans & GitHub) trace-engine-cli trace.json.gz --format md # Show all available subcommands and global flags trace-engine-cli --help ``` ### Global Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `-f, --format` | `'toon' \| 'md'` | `'toon'` | Output serialization format (`toon` or `md`) | | `--time-range` | `string` | — | Filter window relative to trace start (e.g. `"3500,4200"`, `"3.5s,4.2s"`, `"100ms-500ms"`) | | `--absolute-timestamps` | `boolean` | `false` | Treat time ranges as raw absolute trace timestamps rather than relative to trace start | | `--trace-engine`| `string` | — | Path to a custom DevTools trace engine bundle | | `--help` | `boolean` | — | Show help and synopsis | --- ## Relative vs. Absolute Timestamps & Units All time-range inputs (`--time-range`, `--window-a`, `--window-b`, `--bucket`) support: - **Relative timestamps by default**: `0` or `0ms` represents trace start (`bounds.minMs`). `3500` or `3.5s` represents `bounds.minMs + 3500ms`. - **Unit suffixes**: - `s` (seconds): e.g. `3.5s`, `4.2s` - `ms` (milliseconds, default): e.g. `3500ms`, `500` - `us` / `µs` (microseconds): e.g. `3500000us` - **Range formats**: Comma (`"3.5s,4.2s"`), colon (`"3.5s:4.2s"`), range dots (`"3500ms..4200ms"`), or hyphen (`"100ms-500ms"`). - **Absolute mode**: Pass `--absolute-timestamps` to specify raw trace timestamps. --- ## Subcommands ### 1. `overview` (default) High-level trace metadata, Core Web Vitals (FCP, LCP, CLS, INP), non-overlapping main-thread category breakdown (Scripting, Layout, Rendering, GC, System, Idle), and diagnostic warnings. ```bash # Default invocation (includes the drill-down commands footer) trace-engine-cli trace.json.gz # Explicit subcommand (omits the drill-down commands footer) trace-engine-cli overview trace.json.gz ``` **Example TOON Output (`trace-engine-cli trace.json.gz`):** ```yaml bounds: minMs: 122410994.89 maxMs: 122416385.85 durationMs: 5390.96 mainUrl: "https://web.dev/" navigationStartMs: 122410996.89 coreWebVitals: fcp: valueMs: 129.21 rating: good lcp: valueMs: 129.21 rating: good url: "https://web-dev.imgix.net/image/example.svg" cls: value: 0 rating: good worstClusterScore: null inp: null mainThreadBreakdown: scriptingMs: 1.69 layoutMs: 80.13 renderingMs: 17.9 gcMs: 0.07 systemMs: 233.52 idleMs: 5057.64 totalMs: 5390.96 warnings[1]: 1 render-blocking resource(s) detected. # Drill-down commands: # - trace-engine-cli insights [--category ] [--navigation ] # - trace-engine-cli tasks [--min-duration ] [--tree ] [--top ] # - trace-engine-cli find --function [--time-range ] # - trace-engine-cli profile [--time-range ] [--bucket ] # - trace-engine-cli diff --window-a --window-b # - trace-engine-cli scheduling [--time-range ] # - trace-engine-cli network [--render-blocking] [--slowest ] [--initiator-chain ] # - trace-engine-cli interactions # - trace-engine-cli shifts [--events] # - trace-engine-cli events [--name ] [--cat ] [--fields ] # - trace-engine-cli navigations # # Multi-file search: # - trace-engine-cli scan [--name ] [--cat ] [--grep ] ``` --- ### 2. `insights` Extracts actionable diagnostic insight cards generated by Chrome DevTools Insight models. ```bash # All insights trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz # Filter by diagnostic category trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category lcp trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category inp trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category cls trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category render-blocking trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --category third-parties # Target a specific navigation ID or InsightSet ID trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --navigation NAVIGATION_0 trace-engine-cli insights trace.json.gz --navigation 9E74B39B7C378297071F6E3618C4BC14 ``` --- ### 3. `tasks` Main thread task execution, long tasks, and aggregated call trees. ```bash # List long tasks above 50ms (default) trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz # Custom duration threshold and limit within relative window trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz --min-duration 20 --time-range "1s,4s" --top 10 # Bottom-up call tree (aggregated and sorted by self-time) trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz --tree bottom-up --top 20 # Top-down call tree (aggregated and sorted by total duration) trace-engine-cli tasks trace.json.gz --tree top-down --top 20 ``` --- ### 4. `find` Search for executions of a specific function name or pattern to verify call frequency, duration, or confirm starvation (0 calls in window). ```bash # Search for invocations of a function across the whole trace trace-engine-cli find trace.json.gz --function "drawEventTiles" # Query within a specific relative time window trace-engine-cli find trace.json.gz --function "drawEventTiles" --time-range "3.5s,4.2s" ``` --- ### 5. `profile` Time-bucketed CPU profiling progression across discrete slices (e.g. 50ms buckets) to analyze temporal shifts in CPU consumption during gestures. ```bash # Profile with automatic bucket sizing trace-engine-cli profile trace.json.gz --time-range "3.5s,4.1s" # Specify 50ms bucket slices and top 5 functions per slice trace-engine-cli profile trace.json.gz --time-range "3500ms,4100ms" --bucket 50ms --top 5 ``` --- ### 6. `diff` Differential CPU profiling comparing non-overlapping time windows in the trace (e.g. stalled gesture window vs healthy recovery window). ```bash trace-engine-cli diff trace.json.gz --window-a "3.55s,4.0s" --window-b "4.0s,4.45s" --top 10 ``` --- ### 7. `scheduling` Inspects async task and animation frame scheduling lifecycle (`requestAnimationFrame`, `setTimeout`), detecting cancellation rates and rAF/timer thrashing. ```bash # Async task metrics for the full trace trace-engine-cli scheduling trace.json.gz # Narrow to a specific relative interaction window trace-engine-cli scheduling trace.json.gz --time-range "3.5s,4.1s" ``` --- ### 8. `network` Network request waterfall, priority, timings (Queueing, DNS, SSL, TTFB, Download), and request initiator chains. ```bash # Top 20 slowest requests trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --slowest 20 # Filter render-blocking resources only trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --render-blocking # Inspect the upstream initiator chain for a request (by requestId or URL) trace-engine-cli network trace.json.gz --initiator-chain "analytics.js" ``` --- ### 9. `interactions` Inspects user interaction latencies (Interaction to Next Paint - INP), broken down into input delay, processing duration, and presentation delay with target DOM node selectors. ```bash trace-engine-cli interactions trace.json.gz ``` --- ### 10. `shifts` Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) session window clusters, cumulative scores, and culprit DOM elements causing visual instability. Pass `--events` to include individual shift event payloads, navigation IDs, and impacted DOM nodes. ```bash # Cluster summary trace-engine-cli shifts trace.json.gz # Include individual shift events and impacted node debug names trace-engine-cli shifts trace.json.gz --events ``` --- ### 11. `events` Inspect and filter raw trace events directly without custom parsing scripts. Supports filtering by event name, category, phase, time range, and projecting arbitrary nested payload fields via dot-notation: ```bash # Match specific event names trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --name LayoutShift,navigationStart # Extract specific dot-notation payload fields trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --name LayoutShift --fields args.data.navigationId,args.data.is_main_frame # Filter by category and phase trace-engine-cli events trace.json.gz --cat devtools.timeline --phase X --top 20 ``` --- ### 12. `navigations` (alias: `navs`) Inspect all navigations in the trace, their primary main frame status, and their mapped Chrome DevTools Trace Engine `InsightSet` IDs: ```bash trace-engine-cli navigations trace.json.gz ``` --- ### 13. `scan` Scan multiple trace files, directories, or glob patterns for specific events, categories, phases, raw text substrings, or payload property existence. Uses fast string pre-filtering before JSON parsing for rapid discovery across hundreds of test fixtures without loading heavy trace engine pipelines: ```bash # Scan a directory for a specific event name trace-engine-cli scan front_end/panels/timeline/fixtures/traces/ --name LayoutShift # Find which fixture contains a specific string in event payloads trace-engine-cli scan test/fixtures/ --grep "LayerTreeHostImpl:snapshot" # Scan multiple glob patterns for composite categories trace-engine-cli scan "traces/*.json.gz" --cat devtools.timeline --top 10 # Find traces containing specific payload fields trace-engine-cli scan fixtures/ --name TracingStartedInBrowser --fields args.data.frames ``` --- ## Output Formats ### TOON (Default) [TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation)](https://github.com/toon-format/toon) is a compact, uniform tabular format designed to maximize information density for LLMs. It avoids verbose JSON syntax delimiters while preserving structured typing. ### Markdown (`--format md`) Generates standard GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) tables and summary headings, ideal for terminal viewing or pasting into PR descriptions. --- ## Bundling Local DevTools Trace Engine To run `trace-engine-cli` against the latest Chrome DevTools Trace Engine changes from a local `devtools-frontend` repository without needing Ninja: ```bash DEVTOOLS_PATH=/path/to/devtools-frontend npm run bundle:engine ``` This compiles a zero-dependency bundle into `src/engine/vendor/trace_engine.js`. `trace-engine-cli` will automatically detect and prioritize this local vendor file over the npm module. --- ## Development & Testing ```bash # Install dependencies, build, and link locally npm install npm run build npm link # Run test suite (118+ unit tests via node:test) npm test # Run linter and type-checking (Biome & tsc) npm run check # Auto-format codebase npm run format ``` --- ##
